messages.subject: layer_images() / emit_images()
parts:
Hi all,

I have another unusual use case here - this time wondering if I could use layer_images() or emit_images().

My eventual goal is to use a locally-stored image as the background to a ggvis plot, within the axes area.

Here is my best guess as how to use such an emit or layer:

  df <- data.frame(x = 0, y = 0)

  df %>%
    ggvis(
      x = ~x,
      y = ~y,
      url := "http://www.schneider-electric.com/navigation/images/se_logo.gif",
      baseline := "center",
      align := "center"
    ) %>%
    layer_images()

I know there is not a whole lot of support for this now - could I impose for an example of how to get an image to display? I am happy to hack it from there.

If this is something that is not planned to be supported for a while - no problem.

Thanks as always,

Ian

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: layer_images() / emit_images()
parts:
Hi Ian - 

It looks like vega needs a height and width for image marks. I just pushed a fix to allow those props for images. Now you can do something like this:

df <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = 1:3)
df %>%
  ggvis(x = ~x, y = ~y) %>%
  layer_images(
    width := 100,
    height := 100,
url := "http://www.schneider-electric.com/navigation/images/se_logo.gif",

baseline := "middle",
    align := "center"
)


-Winston

messages.subject: Re: layer_images() / emit_images()
parts:
Hi Winston,

I have another use case for you. We are working on a (we think) neat shiny app - we'll be happy to show it off when it's done.

Part of the app involves a ggvis with two layers: (1) a background image, (2) a grid of rectangles on which a user clicks to choose a rectangle.

We would like to use scaled properties to display the image, i.e. x, x2, y, y2, so that we can translate between the image coordinates and the rectangle coordinates. It may be a further challenge to set the aspect ratio of the grid so as not to distort the image (any advice here?).

We have tried to translate the image into greyscale values, then to display as rectangles, but this was a bit slow and heavy.

In short, can the x2 and y2 properties for layer_image() be activated?

Code below.

Thanks as always,

Ian

img_size <- c(142, 60)
img_url <- "http://www.schneider-electric.com/navigation/images/se_logo.gif"

fn_grid <- function(img_size, nx, ny){
  
  dx <- img_size[1] / nx
  dy <- img_size[2] / ny
    
  x = dx * seq(0, nx - 1)  
  y = dy * seq(0, ny - 1)
  
  x_rep <- rep(x, times = ny)
  y_rep <- rep(y, each = ny)
  
  df <- data.frame(
    x_min = x_rep, 
    y_min = y_rep, 
    x_max = x_rep + dx, 
    y_max = y_rep + dy
  ) 

}

df_grid <- fn_grid(img_size, 2, 2)
df_img <- fn_grid(img_size, 1, 1)

# this works
df_img %>%
  ggvis(x = ~x_min, y = ~y_max, x2 = ~x_max, y2 = ~y_min) %>%
  layer_rects(fillOpacity := 0.5) %>%
  layer_rects(stroke := "red", fillOpacity := 0, data = df_grid)

# would like this to work similarly 
df_img %>%
  ggvis(x = ~x_min, y = ~y_max, x2 = ~x_max, y2 = ~y_min) %>%
  layer_images(
    url := "http://www.schneider-electric.com/navigation/images/se_logo.gif"
  ) %>%
  layer_rects(stroke := "red", fillOpacity := 0, data = df_grid)

messages.subject: Re: layer_images() / emit_images()
parts: Oh, I also forgot to mention - for sizing, you could hide the axes, use expand=0 on the scales, and use a specific width:

df_img %>%
  ggvis(x = ~x_min, y = ~y_max, x2 = ~x_max, y2 = ~y_min) %>%
  layer_images(
    url := "http://www.schneider-electric.com/navigation/images/se_logo.gif"
  ) %>%

layer_rects(stroke := "red", fillOpacity := 0, data = df_grid) %>%
  scale_numeric("x", expand = 0) %>%
  scale_numeric("y", expand = 0) %>%
  hide_axis("x") %>%
  hide_axis("y") %>%
  set_options(width = 600, height = 400, keep_aspect = TRUE)

One last (hopefully) question for this thread -

To make things reproducible, I used a public url for the image.

I tried to use an image on my local filesystem, and it does not appear on the plot (and no message). 

In theory, would layer_images(url := file.path("data", "foo.jpg")) be the right syntax, where the path is relative to the working directory?

If we can use public URL's only, that's OK. 

Thanks,

Ian

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: layer_images() / emit_images()
parts:
Local files will require a bit more machinery, since the string can't just be put in the spec; ggvis would also need to copy the file to the right place. This would be different from how all other props operate.

For the time being, only external URLs will work. If you could file an issue, that would be helpful.

-Winston
